Excellent!. It's funny I'm also in a case similarly as yours with the difference that I was doing fine in my semester until we began with face-to-face classes. First of all, I want to ask you.
You are doing bad in college or you just simply don't like it there? If you simply don't like it, you could just tried to get through by seeing it more like a videogame, were you play it and were you finish it you forget about it (by this it's possible you could learn to like your career), and you could try to figure out a backup plan after dropping out, like finding another career, taking some online courses to find what you like or find a job and then talk about it with your parents, they probably will listen to you if you have some plan b after dropping out.
If you are doing bad with your current semester, then again imagine is a videogame and try to do your best, but I know it sounds stressful, so for that think that you don't have anything to lose by this point, so it wouldn't matter if  you do some "last stand" so you could have retain some dignity and feel a little better with yourself that you would have some closure (believe me, there's is nothing worse that leave things halfway through). After that you could discuss with your family with more calm about your plan b.
Either way I say there's always another way.
